name: The Táin Route
description: Approximate interpretive route of Medb's army from Rathcroghan (Cruachan) east to the Cooley Peninsula. This is a scholarly reconstruction — the Táin's exact geography is debated and some locations are symbolic rather than precise. Key stopping points are derived from the text; intermediate waypoints are approximate.
source: Táin Bó Cúailnge (Book of the Dun Cow recension)

waypoints.name: Rathcroghan (Cruachan)
waypoints.description: Start of the march — Medb and Ailill muster the armies of Connacht.

waypoints.name: Shannon Crossing
waypoints.description: The army crosses the Shannon near Carrick-on-Shannon — entering Leinster/Ulster territory.

waypoints.name: Granard — Co. Longford
waypoints.description: Through the midlands — first skirmishes with Ulster scouts.

waypoints.name: Westmeath Crossing
waypoints.description: Through the plain of Westmeath — scouts report Ulster's debility, the march continues.

waypoints.name: Meath — towards Ulster border
waypoints.description: Approaching Ulster — Cú Chulainn begins his single-combat defence of the fords.

waypoints.name: Áth Fhirdia (Ford of Ferdia)
waypoints.description: The climactic four-day duel between Cú Chulainn and Ferdia mac Daman.

waypoints.name: Dún Dealgan — Muirthemne Plain
waypoints.description: Cú Chulainn's home territory — the army reaches the borders of Cooley.

waypoints.name: Cuailnge (Cooley Peninsula)
waypoints.description: Objective reached — the Brown Bull is taken. Ulster warriors begin to recover from the curse.
